rows.episode_title: Pizza Please / Pineapple Pat
rows.synopsis: Harvey and Jinja try to help Robin be patient while waiting for a lunchtime treat. Harvey is excited to adopt a new pet.
rows.situation: The pizza restaurant is full, the rule is wait outside, and Robin wants pizza now, pizza pizza pizza. Every distraction lasts a minute before the wanting comes back, and one more sneak toward the door costs them the table: Dennis says find somewhere else to eat.
rows.coping: Harvey flips the problem: instead of stopping Robin from thinking about pizza, he helps her think about it, and her own pizza song turns waiting into a game. The song is still going when the table opens, and Dennis cooks a pizza shaped like the friend who waited.
rows.notes: mixed age: the pizza song plays 2-4 first and last; the flip from fighting the feeling to riding it out is the tag lesson for the parent searching waiting/impatience. script_vs_synopsis: 'try to help Robin be patient' omits the song-that-works and the almost-losing-the-table stakes. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Robin can smell the pizza, and the restaurant is full. Waiting outside is the rule, but Robin's whole body is pizza, until Harvey notices something: when Robin is thinking about pizza, she is waiting. A made-up pizza song turns her craving into verses, questions, and giggles, the table finally opens, and the pizza that arrives is shaped like Robin herself, extra special for the friend who waited.

rows.episode_title: Pizza Please / Pineapple Pat
rows.synopsis: Harvey and Jinja try to help Robin be patient while waiting for a lunchtime treat. Harvey is excited to adopt a new pet.
rows.situation: Harvey's new pet is a squeaky pineapple named Pat, and Jinja says out loud what everyone can see, that is just a squeaky pineapple. Pat ruins catch, loses the kite, and tells a joke nobody gets, and Jinja does not like playing with Pat, she is not fun for me.
rows.coping: Harvey asks Jinja for one thing, time with Pat just the two of them, and the story gives it a whole song: shared snacks, a book about a tree, popcorn. Jinja comes back having found lots to like, and the seven-catch streak lands with Pat in the game.
rows.notes: mixed age: squeak and slapstick play 2-4; deciding someone is no fun before knowing them, and being wrong, is the 5-7 carry. script_vs_synopsis: 'Harvey is excited to adopt a new pet' hides that the story is Jinja's, and that the turn is one-on-one time, not a lecture. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Pineapple Pat arrives by delivery and Harvey is smitten, but Jinja can see she is a squeaky pineapple who cannot catch, cannot hold a kite string, and tells jokes that land flat. Jinja says Pat is not fun for her, so Harvey asks for one favor, an afternoon with Pat alone. What starts as a favor ends in friendship, and the catch streak that failed all day finally reaches seven with Pat right in the middle of it.

rows.episode_title: Twinkle Toes / Cozy Fort
rows.synopsis: After struggling to learn Jinja's dance, Harvey tries to find his own groove. Jinja inspires Harvey to keep trying new things.
rows.situation: Jinja's new dance is phenomenal and Harvey keeps flopping at it: his tail wags him over, his ears blind him, his legs will not jump a flip. Everyone else can do it, even Jack, and Harvey quits on the spot, no, I do not.
rows.coping: Fins refuses to say keep trying and tells the truth instead: your body moves in a different way, everybody's does. Harvey goes back and does not master Jinja's dance, he makes his own, a Harvey dance with the ears and tail built in, and it is phenomenal.
rows.notes: mixed age: the flop comedy plays 2-4; the difference between keep trying and find your own way is the lesson for kids who cannot do the thing everyone else can. script_vs_synopsis: 'tries to find his own groove' hides the quit-then-return arc and Fins' reframe that the problem was never effort. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Harvey wants to do Jinja's phenomenal new dance, and his body keeps voting no: tail knocks him down, ears cover his eyes, flips stay out of reach. A retreat to the pond ends not with try harder but with something truer, from a fish who gets around on his tail, that everybody moves in different ways. Harvey returns with a dance that is nobody's but his, tail and ears and all, and the whole town dances along.

rows.episode_title: Twinkle Toes / Cozy Fort
rows.synopsis: After struggling to learn Jinja's dance, Harvey tries to find his own groove. Jinja inspires Harvey to keep trying new things.
rows.situation: Jinja builds a cozy fort for one, built for one me, and Harvey builds his own out of treats. It is cozy, and delicious, and something does not feel right: the quiet inside a fort built for one is bigger than the fort.
rows.coping: Harvey cannot name it at first, then says it anyway, that something does not feel right, and Jinja comes over with yarn. One friend becomes every friend, and when the forts all crash together the pieces become one big fort, built for everybody.
rows.notes: mixed age: fort building and silly faces play 2-4; the discovery that cozy-for-one is lonelier than it sounds lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'Harvey tries to find his own groove' is the other story; this one's spine is the lonely fort that ends up big enough for everyone. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Jinja's cozy fort is perfect for one, and Harvey copies it with snack walls, then discovers the flaw no snack can fix: alone is quiet. He admits something does not feel right, and the visitors keep arriving until a ruckus collapses every fort in Sagoville into one heap of parts. Harvey sees the pile and sees an answer, the coziest fort ever, big enough for all of them.

rows.episode_title: Piece of Cake / X Marks the Spot
rows.synopsis: As Harvey and Jinja bake a cake for Remy, a small mistake leads to a big problem. Harvey and Robin play in a new fort.
rows.situation: Remy's winter party has no cake, so his friends volunteer to bake one, and Remy gives the exact spec: vanilla, white frosting, white sprinkles, big. Harvey remembers the big part and adds pinch after pinch of growing powder, and the perfect cake keeps growing out of the kitchen, across the floor, and out of reach of the party.
rows.coping: Harvey says it himself before anyone else can, I added a lot, and owns the mistake out loud to Remy. The fix is a flip: they cannot bring the cake to the party, so the whole conga line brings the party to the cake.
rows.notes: mixed age: the runaway-cake musical plays 2-4; a mistake made with good intentions, said out loud and fixed sideways, is the tag lesson for making mistakes. script_vs_synopsis: 'a small mistake leads to a big problem' is the spine; the script adds that Remy's own instructions fed the mistake, and that his thank you comes before he has even seen the cake. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Remy's winter party needs one thing, and the bakery has none, so Harvey and Jinja bake from his exact wish list. Then Harvey adds a teensy bit more growing powder, then a pinch for every friend on the guest list, and the cake outgrows the house while the party waits. He tells Remy the truth, the conga line reroutes to Harvey's kitchen, and the biggest, sparkliest, most wonderfully wintry cake in Sagoville serves everyone one super tasty piece.

rows.episode_title: Piece of Cake / X Marks the Spot
rows.synopsis: As Harvey and Jinja bake a cake for Remy, a small mistake leads to a big problem. Harvey and Robin play in a new fort.
rows.situation: Jack turns up at the beach in full pirate kit on a treasure quest, digs up a real chest, and finds it empty. A pirate without treasure is no pirate at all, so the hat, jacket, beard, eye patch, and compass come off piece by piece, and even pirate underwear.
rows.coping: Harvey names the heartbreak out loud, that opening the empty chest broke his heart, and the friends answer by building Jack a brand new quest: a homemade map, a chest buried by pirates they know, and treasure inside this time. The shell and the fruit basket prove he was a pirate all along.
rows.notes: mixed age: the dig and the songs play 2-4; a friend's dream deflating, and rebuilding it yourself for them, is the 5-7 carry. script_vs_synopsis: 'Harvey and Robin play in a new fort' is a different story entirely, the catalog synopsis pairs to the other half; tags are anchored on segment_title and the script. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Jack arrives a pirate and leaves the beach undressed, hat, jacket, beard, and dignity stripped off layer by layer after an empty treasure chest. Harvey and the crew will not let the dream die in a hole: they draw their own map, recruit Umi to bury a chest, and send Jack on one more X-marked adventure made of friends. What he digs up is real this time, and so is the pirate he stayed.

rows.episode_title: Harvey's Wild Ride / Fintastic Adventure
rows.synopsis: When Harvey and Jack visit Alan's house, they end up on an adventure through space. Harvey joins a magical quest.
rows.situation: Alan's spaceship house is a wonder of unlabeled buttons, and Alan cannot remember what any of them do. Harvey and Jack launch a helpful project, push a button, put a sticky picture on, until one push starts the whole ship shaking and another launches them into outer space with no way home.
rows.coping: The panic has a method: they name the problem, hunt the seat eject button in a pond, and ring Alan's doorbell, in space, to confess. Alan is delighted rather than upset, the labeling gets finished with the sticky picture maker, and the last untried button turns out to be the Sagoville button.
rows.notes: mixed age: the space romp plays 2-4; helpfulness that outruns permission, and the apology that fixes it, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'end up on an adventure through space' omits that the trip starts as a labeling project for a forgetful friend and ends in a confession at a space doorbell. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Alan's buttons baffle even Alan, so Harvey and Jack volunteer to test every single one and label it with a sticky picture. The project works beautifully until one button shakes the ship and another fires them past planets with no Sagoville button in sight. A soaked seat-eject recovery, a sheepish doorbell confession, and one more untried button later, everyone is home, the labels are on, and the spaceship crew shares alien cereal.

rows.episode_title: Harvey's Wild Ride / Fintastic Adventure
rows.synopsis: When Harvey and Jack visit Alan's house, they end up on an adventure through space. Harvey joins a magical quest.
rows.situation: Fins has trained all season for his biggest-ever dive off the biggest-ever waterfall, and every pinecone family, salamander, and sparkle spring on the trail pulls Harvey's eyes sideways. The detours cost them the one cable car, and the dive Fins prepared for does not happen.
rows.coping: Fins says the truth without meanness, we missed it, then lets Harvey turn the day around: the acorn Nutmeg dropped is worth chasing. The squirrel chase they almost skipped becomes the best part, and Nutmeg's flying squirrel plane still gets Fins to his dive.
rows.notes: mixed age: the squirrel chase plays 2-4; two friends with different paces meeting in the middle, and a missed big moment being survived, land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'Harvey joins a magical quest' is the other story's line; tags anchor on segment_title plus the script. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Fins is focused and Harvey is a firehose of wonder, and their walk to the biggest-ever dive is a tug of war between the two. Every detour Harvey loves costs time, and the missed cable car costs Fins his dive, a quiet, honest disappointment. Then one dropped acorn turns the day: the chase to return it is the adventure neither planned, and a flying squirrel named Nutmeg delivers them both to the waterfall after all.

rows.episode_title: Home with Herb / Follow That Squeak
rows.synopsis: Alan asks Harvey to care for his plant, Herb. Harvey loses his beloved ball and travels around Sagoville chasing its squeak.
rows.situation: Alan asks Harvey to plant-sit Herb, one very important instruction forgotten on the way out the door. Herb looks sad, and Harvey pulls out everything that makes Harvey happy, squeaky toys, the playground, the merry-go-round, and Herb stays sad through all of it.
rows.coping: Harvey refuses to fake it: sorry Herb, I really wanted to take good care of you, but I just do not know how. The friends consult Jinja's plant books and try dirt, sun, and water first, and the answer arrives by accident, Herb lights up when Harvey picks him up.
rows.notes: mixed age: playground musical numbers play 2-4; doing your best for someone in your care and asking what they actually need, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'Alan asks Harvey to care for his plant' omits the whole wrong-playground-right-plant arc and the forgotten instruction, which Alan remembers at the end: Herb likes to be held. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Harvey takes plant-sitting seriously, and Herb will not cheer up no matter how much fun the playground has to offer. The friends research like pros, dirt parties, beach towels for sunshine, a rain dance, and the plant stays droopy, until Harvey admits he does not know how to care for Herb at all. The answer was in Harvey's arms the whole time, and Alan returns to build an Herb Holder so the holding can be official.

rows.episode_title: Home with Herb / Follow That Squeak
rows.synopsis: Alan asks Harvey to care for his plant, Herb. Harvey loses his beloved ball and travels around Sagoville chasing its squeak.
rows.situation: Harvey's very best, most favorite squeaky ball vanishes mid-fetch, and every squeak in Sagoville sounds like it: Hugbot's arms, Blueberry's wheel, Wilson's needles, a caterpillar deejay. Each false lead is a friend, and the trail keeps moving.
rows.coping: Harvey says the hard sentence, I think my ball is gone forever, and keeps going anyway. The friends build the rescue out of what everyone brought, a tricycle wheel, knitting needles, and Larry's missing poster, and Jack's eyes find the ball up Harvey's own tree.
rows.notes: mixed age: the squeak chase plays 2-4; persisting after grief says quit, with the whole town's help, is the tag lesson for losing something precious. script_vs_synopsis: 'travels around Sagoville chasing its squeak' is right; the script adds the chain of friendly false squeaks and the team-built ball rescue machine. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Harvey's favorite squeaky ball flies off the bat and disappears, and Sagoville is suddenly full of squeaks that are not it. The search turns into a town-wide musical, everyone Harvey meets squeaks for a living, and hope thins out until Harvey says the words, gone forever. Then Jack spots orange and stripy in the tree, and a rescue machine cobbled from a trike wheel, knitting needles, and pure friendship brings the very best, most favorite ball home.

rows.episode_title: Gary's New Horn / Harvey Gets the Scoop
rows.synopsis: Harvey joins Gary on a magical quest to meet the Horn Fairy. Dennis leaves Harvey in charge of his ice-cream truck.
rows.situation: Gary's horn falls off, and the road to the Horn Fairy runs into a wall, a grumpy bridge-builder, and a lost butterfly named Tonk. Gary can no longer make rainbows, the thing his old horn was for, and watches the quest need exactly what he feels he has lost.
rows.coping: Gary keeps offering the horn he thinks is worthless, an ear-scratcher, a telescope, a salon for Hildi's hair, and grumpy feelings get chased away one helper at a time. At the fairy's door the truth comes out: the old horn was not done bringing happiness, and the new horn it earns makes the biggest rainbow of his life.
rows.notes: mixed age: the rainbow salon and horn ball play 2-4; losing the thing that made you special, and finding you still are, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'a magical quest to meet the Horn Fairy' omits that the whole quest is powered by the horn Gary believes is broken. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Gary's beloved horn falls off, and the only cure is a quest to the Horn Fairy with the old horn in hand. Every obstacle on the way needs something Gary cannot do anymore, rainbows, until he discovers what a horn without rainbows can do: scratch an unreachable itch, find lost butterflies, curl a grump's hair, win at horn ball. The fairy takes the old horn with full honors, and the magnificent new one that replaces it spends its first minute making the biggest rainbow Gary has ever made.

rows.episode_title: Gary's New Horn / Harvey Gets the Scoop
rows.synopsis: Harvey joins Gary on a magical quest to meet the Horn Fairy. Dennis leaves Harvey in charge of his ice-cream truck.
rows.situation: Dennis closes the ice-cream truck to help at the pizza restaurant and hands Harvey the scoop, the steps, and a flavor map that defies memory. The customers keep coming with orders like pancake ice cream, seven brumble berries, fifteen sprinkles, and every order comes back wrong.
rows.coping: Harvey keeps saying the true thing under the chaos, being an ice-cream scooper is really hard, and lets Jinja's drawings help even after the drawings fail. The wrong orders become the Harvey Surprise, the most delicious creation his customers have ever tasted.
rows.notes: emoji note: replaced a non-emoji token with standard set. mixed age: flavor comedy plays 2-4; drowning in a job that looked easy, and letting mistakes become the specialty, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'Dennis leaves Harvey in charge' omits Remy's impossible order, the failed picture menus, and that the signature sundae is invented by accident. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Harvey's dream job comes with three easy steps and one impossible memory: freezer five has cheese, freezer six has toothpaste and lime, and there is no freezer two. The orders pile up wrong, the picture menus do not save him, and Harvey admits scooping is really hard. Then the mistakes start tasting delicious, the Harvey Surprise goes on the menu by accident, and Dennis comes back to a truck full of happy customers.

rows.episode_title: Mysterious Mess-Maker / Muddy Harvey
rows.synopsis: Someone is making messes around Sagoville, and Harvey and Jack are ready to find some answers! Blueberry Monster makes her debut.
rows.situation: A perfect block tower crashes the second their backs turn, and a blue hair in the photo turns the cleanup into a manhunt. The trail of messes gets bigger, Jinja's library, Robin's toy bath, paint and eggs, until the blue mess-maker is cornered.
rows.coping: Blueberry Monster gets asked why instead of yelled at, and the why is simple: her hair is so long it covers her eyes, and she cannot see a thing she knocks over. The friends get her a haircut, hand back a town already tidied, and rebuild the tower together with their mystery guest.
rows.notes: mixed age: the chase numbers play 2-4; the lesson that a culprit is usually a problem you have not asked about yet, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'ready to find some answers' hides that the mess-maker is a nearsighted monster mid-haircut-quest, and that the kids had already cleaned most of her messes for her. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: The tallest block tower ever falls with no one near it, and a blue hair in the snapshot makes it a case. Harvey and Jack chase the mess across Sagoville, one toppled library and one saved rubber ducky later, and find Blueberry Monster, big, blue, and blindly bumping into everything because her hair hangs over her eyes. One haircut at Hugbot's later, the messes are explained, mostly cleaned by the friends themselves, and the tower goes back up taller with the mess-maker on the team.

rows.episode_title: Mysterious Mess-Maker / Muddy Harvey
rows.synopsis: Someone is making messes around Sagoville, and Harvey and Jack are ready to find some answers! Blueberry Monster makes her debut.
rows.situation: Harvey is too muddy to play tag, basketball, or tea party, and every friend offers the same deal, a bath first. He shops for a friend who does not mind the mud, comes up empty, and declares he will stay by himself, forever, because he does not want the fix everyone is offering.
rows.coping: Robin does the thing Harvey cannot, helps him get clean, and the crew turns the bath he refused into a playtime bath party with a waterslide and supersized bubbles. He plays with everyone and gets clean at the same time, which was the only deal in town all along.
rows.notes: mixed age: the Rub-A-Dub Clean Club number plays 2-4; digging in when everyone says the same thing, and the friend who helps anyway, land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'ready to find some answers' is the other story; tags anchor on segment_title plus the script. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Harvey comes out of tag one giant mud splat, and playtime closes everywhere he goes: too muddy for Jinja, for Jack, for tea parties, for swinging. He would rather search the whole town than take a bath, and the search ends with nobody to play with and a very clean-looking forever alone. Robin quietly starts helping him wash, and the friends reroute the whole argument into a Good-Time Rub-A-Dub Clean Club party, where getting clean is the game.

rows.episode_title: Creative Campout / Boingy Bear
rows.synopsis: Larry the Log helps Harvey and Jack with their camping trip. Harvey, Jinja, and Jack try to cheer up Robin.
rows.situation: The first-ever camping trip is planned by a dog who packed squeaky toys, a flag, and lots of underwear, and a rabbit who packed carrots. Campsite 4 is real and so is the dark, and there is no flashlight, tent, or sleeping bag in either backpack.
rows.coping: Larry the Log teaches the whole fix in one line, you did not bring it, but you can wing it: a branch becomes a shovel, an empty backpack becomes a sleeping bag, toilet paper becomes a pillow, and a carrot becomes a campfire. The trip they almost skipped becomes the best one yet.
rows.notes: mixed age: the wing-it song plays 2-4; the gap between the camping trip you imagined and the one you can actually have, closed by imagination, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'Larry the Log helps Harvey and Jack with their camping trip' omits the packing-list comedy and that every missing supply gets reimagined on the spot. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Harvey and Jack arrive at their first campsite with flag, squeaky toys, underwear, and carrots, and discover they brought none of the things camping needs. Going home looks certain until Larry the Log reframes the whole trip: anything at all is just a thing, and the forest provides the rest if you wing it. Stick-shovel, backpack-bed, rainbow bench, carrot campfire, and the unprepared campers have the coziest night in Sagoville.

rows.episode_title: Creative Campout / Boingy Bear
rows.synopsis: Larry the Log helps Harvey and Jack with their camping trip. Harvey, Jinja, and Jack try to cheer up Robin.
rows.situation: Robin has a sore wing and has to stay inside, and her friends keep failing to cheer her: the comic book hole is buried in snow, and the Boingy Bear snow statue they build slides off down the hill the moment it is finished. Boingy Bear cannot save anyone from the window Robin watches from.
rows.coping: Nobody fakes the fix: the snow bear runs off and the friends say so, no, we do not have anything to cheer up Robin now. But the runaway statue did save a snow cone and block a snowball on its way, Robin saw her hero be a hero from her window, and the dress-up Boingy Bear show finishes the job inside.
rows.notes: mixed age: the boinging statue plays 2-4; a friend stuck inside while everyone plays, and cheering that has to adapt to where she actually is, land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'Harvey, Jinja, and Jack try to cheer up Robin' omits the two failed attempts and that the third one works by pure accident before the planned show. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Robin's sore wing benches her by the window, and her friends audition ways to reach her: a buried comic hole yields nothing but an old scarf, and their magnificent Boingy Bear snow statue immediately slides off downhill. The rescue looks ruined, until Robin reports what she saw out the window, her hero catching snow cones and blocking snowballs mid-slide. A dress-up show inside finishes what the statue started, and the friend who could not come out gets the whole adventure brought in.

rows.episode_title: Abraca-Blooey / The Great Skate
rows.synopsis: Harvey's favorite fetching stick gets swapped with Peanuts' magic wand. Harvey, Jack and Robin attend magic training.
rows.situation: Mr. Stickles, the very best fetching stick, tastes wrong and is a lot less fetch-y, because he is Peanuts' magic wand. The swap has magic words in it: any word but abraca-blooey causes trouble, and the trouble multiplies with every guess, flying pizzas, extra shoes, pigs, then flying blue pigs.
rows.coping: Harvey keeps trying long after the guesses run out, remembers the real magic word mid-chaos, and stops the wand. The apology is a cleanup, wand, fix all the trouble we caused, and ends with both treasures back where they belong, plus wigs for everyone at the show.
rows.notes: mixed age: the wrong-word chaos plays 2-4; owning a mess you did not quite mean to make, and undoing it piece by piece, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'Harvey's favorite fetching stick gets swapped with Peanuts' magic wand' is right; the script adds the near-magic-word escalation ladder and the wand-runaway chase. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Harvey fetches the wrong stick home from the park, and Mr. Stickles turns out to be a magic wand with one true magic word and a taste for disaster when anyone guesses wrong. A rescue mission to the magic show turns into flying pizza, multiplying pigs, and one remembered word, abraca-blooey, that stops it all. The wand is returned with a full cleanup spell, Mr. Stickles is restored to fetching duty, and Peanuts' show gets the wiggliest audience of all.

rows.episode_title: Abraca-Blooey / The Great Skate
rows.synopsis: Harvey's favorite fetching stick gets swapped with Peanuts' magic wand. Harvey, Jack and Robin attend magic training.
rows.situation: Harvey surprises his friends with roller skates and helmets, and Jinja keeps falling before the very first glide. She sits the skating out, I do not think I will ever be able to roller-skate, and decides to watch from the sidelines instead.
rows.coping: The lessons go straight, turn, stop, and the stopping never quite stops. Then Harvey gets stuck in a cloud and Jinja skates a full rescue without falling once, straight, turn, stop, everything she learned, at speed, and the skirt of the pond sees she has been skating the whole time.
rows.notes: mixed age: the skate lessons play 2-4; learning that will not stick until it suddenly does, and courage found mid-rescue, land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'Harvey, Jack and Robin attend magic training' is the other story; tags anchor on segment_title plus the script. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Jinja wants skating to be stupendous and her body keeps voting ground, go straight falls, turn falls, even stopping flops. She retires to the sidelines until Harvey's cloud rescue demands a skater, and she skates it without a single fall, having learned more than she knew. The rescue makes her a skater in everyone's eyes before she can decide she is not one.

rows.episode_title: Wedding Wednesday / Don't Touch the Ground
rows.synopsis: Harvey and friends add personal touches to Tom and Astrid's weekly wedding. Jinja and Harvey compare their friendship favorites.
rows.situation: Tom and Astrid get married every Wednesday to celebrate each other, a small ritual with a song, a hat swap, and a whirl. One by one the friends add firsts they mean well: a harp, decorations, capes, a flower girl, a fruitcake, and the sky opens mid-song on the whole unschooled production.
rows.coping: Tom reframes before panic wins, we can still have Wedding Wednesday, we just need something to keep us dry. Gary's wedding rainbow clears the rain, and the littlest gnome wedding becomes the biggest one they have had, every first kept and none of the ritual lost.
rows.notes: mixed age: the wedding song plays 2-4; tradition getting loved a little too hard by helpers, and coming out bigger, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'add personal touches to Tom and Astrid's weekly wedding' is the spine; the script adds the rainstorm near-disaster and that the couple welcome every addition before it backfires. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Every Wednesday, two gnomes get married again, on purpose, because they are best friends and it is Wednesday. Harvey signs on as official hat swapper and the whole town stacks on firsts, harp music, decorations, capes, flower girl, fruitcake, right up until rain threatens to wash it all out. A wedding rainbow arrives exactly when the ritual needs a roof, and the sweetest small tradition ends up larger, not lost.

rows.episode_title: Wedding Wednesday / Don't Touch the Ground
rows.synopsis: Harvey and friends add personal touches to Tom and Astrid's weekly wedding. Jinja and Harvey compare their friendship favorites.
rows.situation: The ground is lava, or rather goo, and the first cone of ice cream goes to whoever reaches Binky the fastest without touching it. Jinja builds a bucket bridge and Harvey borrows Neville's ball, and the race tightens to a tie until Dennis arrives under a flying ice cream.
rows.coping: Harvey catches the ice cream and loses the game in the same jump, touched ground, stuck in goo, and hands Jinja the win without being asked. Jinja spends her first-cone prize on him, ketchup and dog treats, because he saved the ice cream for everyone.
rows.notes: mixed age: the goo game plays 2-4; a race won by doing the kind thing instead of the fast thing, and a friend who notices, land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'Jinja and Harvey compare their friendship favorites' is the other story; tags anchor on segment_title plus the script. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Dennis runs out of vanilla, and the wait becomes a game: cross the park without touching the goo-covered ground, first one to Binky gets the first cone. Jinja engineers her way there on snack pails, Harvey bounces in on a borrowed ball, and the tie breaks when an ice cream flies: Harvey saves it, loses the race, and declares Jinja the winner on the spot. She trades her prize cone for the right to hand him the first one, ketchup and dog treats, his favorites.

rows.episode_title: Happy Thankful Day
rows.synopsis: When an invention mishap sends Harvey and Robin far from Sagoville, they find ways to be grateful for the unexpected. Alan tests a new invention.
rows.situation: Harvey and Robin get zapped to Lumington, a town with one tree, one wall, a toast truck, and no Thankful Day, while the festival back home goes on without them. Lucy drives the only bus and Leonard has never once been thanked for anything.
rows.coping: Harvey does what he does anywhere: thanks the bench out loud, and the town starts to glow. The friends turn a missed festival into a brand new one, Lumington's own, with rock races, a Thankful Bus for a tree, and two hosts who learned the feeling themselves.
rows.notes: mixed age: the tour-of-nothing comedy plays 2-4; gratitude as a skill you can learn anywhere, and the friends who follow your glow, land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'find ways to be grateful for the unexpected' is the spine; the script adds the zapped-by-invention setup, Lucy's first thank you ever, and that the Sagoville crew finds them by following the glow. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: A here-to-there-inator sends Harvey and Robin nowhere near the top of the Thankful Tree and somewhere named Lumington, while the festival they love happens without them. What the plainer town in the world needs, it turns out, is exactly what Harvey carries: a thank you said out loud, to a bench, that makes Lucy glow. The tour becomes a lesson, the bus becomes a Thankful Tree, and when their friends finally find them, the best Thankful Day ever happens right where they were lost.

rows.episode_title: Treasure It
rows.synopsis: An old lunch box finds new life when Harvey transforms it into a treasure box full of unique items. Harvey discovers a hidden talent.
rows.situation: Harvey's beloved lunch box splits at the seams, and instead of a sad goodbye he reopens it as a treasure box where every friend picks a prize. Then the treasures come out sideways: a sock, cracked spoons, wrapping paper, and nobody can see what any of it is worth.
rows.coping: Each doubt gets answered with a whole adventure story that proves the treasure: a sock parachute in space, cowgirl Jinja's spoons of glory, Sir Robin's wrapping-paper shield. The box is empty by the end, which is the good part, and the friends refill it for Harvey with an egg carton that is definitely a submarine.
rows.notes: mixed age: the story-within-story games play 2-4; finding worth in what looks like trash, and proving value by using it, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'finds new life as a treasure box' omits the doubt-from-friends beat and the story-as-proof structure that carries the whole segment. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Harvey's split lunch box becomes a treasure box, and the treasure is junk until the stories start: a sock that saves two space rangers, cracked spoons that herd calves, wrapping paper that becomes a knight's shield, crown, and key. One by one the friends stop seeing trash and start seeing what a thing can do, and the empty box ends up more valuable full of friends' refills than it ever was full of lunch.

rows.episode_title: New Year's Steve
rows.synopsis: When a firefly named Steve helps grant a New Year's wish, the gang goes on a scavenger hunt. The friends celebrate New Year's Eve with a scavenger hunt.
rows.situation: The friends have fallen asleep before the New Year's bell every single year, and this year Harvey refuses again. Steve the new firefly has never granted a wish, the hunt for ten horns and nine fancy things runs out of stars, and the shooting star slips away at the last second.
rows.coping: Robin says it first: the wish failed, and the night is still really thankful-worthy, they met a firefly, had pizza, made their own surprises. Then the bell rings while everyone is awake anyway, and the year's last surprise is theirs without any magic at all.
rows.notes: mixed age: the countdown hunt plays 2-4; trying hard for a thing that does not come, and finding the night was still enough, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'a firefly named Steve helps grant a New Year's wish' omits that the wish technically fails, and that the kids see the bell awake because the hunt kept them up. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Every New Year's Eve ends the same way in Sagoville, asleep before the bell, so Harvey enlists Steve, a firefly brand new to wish granting, and a twelve-item scavenger hunt to keep everyone awake. The hunt succeeds beautifully right up until it does not, the shooting star is lost, and the wish dies with it. The friends choose thankfulness over disappointment, and the surprise they have missed every year arrives while they are still up, singing about their own.

rows.episode_title: Turkey Tea Party / Jinja's Mystery Package
rows.synopsis: Robin hosts a one-of-a-kind celebration. Harvey leaps into action to save Jinja's surprise from being spoiled.
rows.situation: Robin's turkey tea party runs on rules: dress like a turkey, curtsy like a turkey, say the gobble words, and only then, tea. The rules are tickly, twirly, and dizzy-making, and her friends start to wobble between wanting tea and wanting to keep their dignity.
rows.coping: Nobody sneaks out and nobody mocks the rules: they ask for a different way in, and Robin says yes each time, own costumes, own curtsies, best-effort gobbles. Robin decides the new version is more silly, and turkeys arrive to a party that fits everyone.
rows.notes: mixed age: the gobble song plays 2-4; a host learning her rules can flex without breaking, and guests asking instead of quitting, land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'Robin hosts a one-of-a-kind celebration' omits the three rule-adjustment negotiations that are the whole story. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Robin's turkey tea party has rules, and the rules have opinions: turkey costumes tickle, turkey curtsies cause vertigo, and Harvey's gobble keeps coming out bark. One asked-for change at a time, the party reshapes around the friends instead of losing them, and Robin declares the silly version the best version, with actual turkeys joining the tea.

rows.episode_title: Turkey Tea Party / Jinja's Mystery Package
rows.synopsis: Robin hosts a one-of-a-kind celebration. Harvey leaps into action to save Jinja's surprise from being spoiled.
rows.situation: Harvey peeks at Jinja's mystery package and cannot unpeek: a pretend palm tree escapes its box, the box is ripped, and the surprise he promised not to ruin is standing in the yard in plain sight of a returning Jinja.
rows.coping: Harvey does not shrug, he engineers: a new box from Jack's collection, a failed squish, a costume disguise that fools nobody, and finally wrapping paper, wrapping the whole gang included. Jinja is more surprised than the original plan could have managed, and spends her surprise on a beach party for them.
rows.notes: mixed age: the dress-up-tree gags play 2-4; protecting a surprise for someone else, and the lengths that cost, land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'save Jinja's surprise from being spoiled' hides that Harvey caused the spoil-risk by peeking, and that the fix wraps him inside the package. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: One peek at Jinja's mystery package and the surprise is loose, a squished palm tree, a ripped box, and minutes until Jinja is home. Harvey, Jack, and Robin try a new box, a two-person squish, and a costumed tree before settling on the classic, wrapping paper, with themselves inside the package. Jinja has never been more surprised, and her beach party thanks them for it.

rows.episode_title: All Aboard / Snow Delivery
rows.synopsis: An underground train sparks excitement across Sagoville. Rosie and friends help Harvey with a gift delivery.
rows.situation: Jack's digging for collection space uncovers an underground train station and a mole named Nola building track to the beach. The friends lay rails, the whole town requests stops, and the maiden ride overflows: the train is too small for everyone who helped build it.
rows.coping: The too-small train becomes a puzzle instead of a verdict, and Jack's collections supply the answer, wheels under everything you can sit on, rainbow seat belts included. Everyone rides, including Nola, and the train that went to the beach now goes all over Sagoville.
rows.notes: mixed age: the chugga-chugga numbers play 2-4; building something together and then making room for every builder, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'an underground train sparks excitement' omits Nola, the too-small-train problem, and that the fix comes from Jack's collections. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: A dig for storage room turns into a discovered train station, and Harvey and Jack end up laying track beside Nola the train mole, to the beach, the forest, the market, and the mountaintop. The celebration hit is the seating chart: more builders than seats. Jack's collections turn every ridable object into rolling stock, and the Sagoville choo choo departs with the entire construction crew aboard.

rows.episode_title: All Aboard / Snow Delivery
rows.synopsis: An underground train sparks excitement across Sagoville. Rosie and friends help Harvey with a gift delivery.
rows.situation: Harvey wants to send Grandpa Jasper his saved snowball, a very special delivery, and the sun has other plans. The gift shrinks at every stop on Rosie's route, mittens, shade, tunnels, and umbrellas notwithstanding, and the last leg is pure sunlight with no cover left.
rows.coping: Harvey solves the unfixable by mail: he writes the sun a polite letter asking for shade, and the sun obliges. The snowball arrives small and the gift lands big, because it turns out Grandpa Jasper needed exactly that for lemonade.
rows.notes: mixed age: the shade-chase plays 2-4; a gift losing its grandness in transit and still arriving as love, plus writing to the sun, land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'help Harvey with a gift delivery' omits the melt race across four friends' deliveries and the letter to the sun. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Harvey's special delivery for Grandpa Jasper is a snowball he has been saving, and Rosie's sunny delivery route is a slow-motion melt. Every friend on the route lends a fix, mittens, a dark tunnel, an umbrella, giant shade flowers, until the last sunny stretch has no solution except Harvey's: a letter to the sun, politely requesting shade. The snowball arrives small, the grandpa arrives delighted, and the lemonade is perfect.

rows.episode_title: A New Boo Boo / Harvey Rocks
rows.synopsis: Harvey fills in for everyone's favorite prankster. After adopting a houseful of pet rocks, Harvey realizes he may need some help.
rows.situation: Boo Boo the ghost leaves town to visit his grandma, and Harvey volunteer-fills the surpriser job in a bedsheet. Every boo lands flat: friends see him coming, the floating envelope is just his hand, and Remy's superstrong hiccups need a scare Harvey cannot scare.
rows.coping: Harvey keeps adjusting instead of quitting, hiding behind books, popping up unseen, until Dennis laughs anyway, you saw me and you still surprised me. When his own tricks cannot fix Remy's hiccups, he says so, and Boo Boo's return with ghost friends finishes the job.
rows.notes: mixed age: the hiccup gags play 2-4; trying to copy someone else's magic, and learning your own version counts, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'fills in for everyone's favorite prankster' omits the flat-boo failure streak, Dennis's grace note, and the honest handoff when the hiccups outmatch him. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: With Boo Boo the ghost away, Harvey borrows the surpriser job and discovers it is harder in a bedsheet: everyone sees him, nothing floats, and Remy's superstrong hiccups shrug off every boo. A pizza-restaurant surprise he is sure failed gets a laugh anyway, and when the hiccups finally need the real ghost, Harvey says so. Boo Boo returns with reinforcements, the hiccups surrender, and the fill-in learns his own kind of surprise counts.

rows.episode_title: A New Boo Boo / Harvey Rocks
rows.synopsis: Harvey fills in for everyone's favorite prankster. After adopting a houseful of pet rocks, Harvey realizes he may need some help.
rows.situation: A friendly rock with a tail follows Harvey home and becomes Fluffy, the pet rock, feeding time, belly rubs, rock music and all. Then the whole forest follows, and Harvey's house fills with pets he loves and cannot possibly care for alone, baths, walks, and mop required.
rows.coping: Harvey says the sentence pet owners dread, I love them and I really want to take care of them all, but I am not sure I can do it by myself, and the answer is not returning them, it is sharing: each rock leaves for a friend's home, every rock gets a great friend, every friend gets the perfect pet.
rows.notes: mixed age: rock-bath slapstick plays 2-4; the difference between loving something and being able to care for it, and sharing as the loving answer, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'a houseful of pet rocks' omits Fluffy's solo adoption arc, the overload spiral, and that the rocks are rehomed by personality match. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Harvey adopts a tail-wagging pet rock named Fluffy, and the whole forest wants in: one rock becomes a houseful of Mittens, Marshmallow, Pooky-Bear, Shaggy Dave, and Puddles, with bath time to prove it. The fun tips over into too much, and Harvey, who wanted to do it all, says out loud that he cannot do it alone. The rehoming that follows is not giving up, it is matching every rock with the right friend, and the whole crew plays fetch together by the end.

rows.episode_title: Frogbot / Hotdogging Around
rows.synopsis: Hugbot puzzles everyone with a change in personality. Harvey and Juggo team up to move a giant hot dog.
rows.situation: Hugbot, the town's hug distributor, goes strange: no hugs, only hopping, huggit, huggit, and a fly-chasing sprint nobody can catch. Every friend who needs a comfort hug after a tumble gets a bounce instead, and worry spreads through Sagoville.
rows.coping: Robin names the goal before the panic wins, if we do not help, Hugbot will never hug again, and hugging is Hugbot's favorite thing. The clue is a ribbit, and the answer is the tool Hugbot taught them: one group hug, the biggest and group-iest ever, pops the frog out gently.
rows.notes: mixed age: the huggit chase plays 2-4; a friend acting strangely needs help, not judgment, and the fix is meeting them the way they help you, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'a change in personality' hides the frog reveal, the failed boingy-chase, and that the rescue is a giant hug. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Hugbot stops hugging and starts hopping, and Sagoville's comfort economy collapses one bounced friend at a time. The crew chases, puzzles, and finally hears the ribbit: a frog got in, and Hugbot has gone full Frogbot. Impossible chases and stuck doors lose to the town's own medicine, one enormous group hug that frees the frog and returns the hugs.

rows.episode_title: Frogbot / Hotdogging Around
rows.synopsis: Hugbot puzzles everyone with a change in personality. Harvey and Juggo team up to move a giant hot dog.
rows.situation: Juggo's new shoe store sign arrives as a giant hot dog, wrong order, enormous, and suddenly everybody wants lunch. Harvey adopts it, and it will not stay put, plow pushes, airplane lifts, and Alan's half-noodleled ray all lose to a rolling wiener the size of a bus.
rows.coping: Harvey flips the problem at the end: if the hot dog will not be carried, drive it. The whole town bolts on wheels, the hot dog becomes a hot dog car, and the first trip delivers Juggo the shoe sign he actually ordered.
rows.notes: mixed age: the runaway hot dog is 2-4 at full power; the pivot from moving a problem to riding it, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'team up to move a giant hot dog' omits the order mix-up, the parade of failed transport schemes, and the hot dog car finale. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Juggo's shoe store gets a sign shaped like a car-sized hot dog, and Harvey inherits the delivery problem of the year. A plow, a plane, and a misfiring Send-It-Away Ray all fail against a wiener with momentum, until Harvey stops pushing and starts driving: the hot dog becomes a hot dog car. The victory lap ends at the sign store, picking up the giant shoe that says what the store actually sells.

rows.episode_title: Prize Bow Tie / Bread is Sleeping
rows.synopsis: Jack sets his sights on winning a unique prize at the carnival. While Robin's loaf of bread naps, the friends try to keep the noise down.
rows.situation: Jack needs one orange bow tie to complete his collection, and the carnival's ball game keeps handing the prizes to everyone else. Three tickets, three misses, and a string of near winners while Jack's fun quietly drains out of the day.
rows.coping: Harvey asks the question that matters, are you having any fun, and buys Jack back some joy before the last ticket. The final roll is played for fun, the miss is hilarious instead of heartbreaking, and an orange flag picked up on the way out completes the collection anyway.
rows.notes: mixed age: the carnival games play 2-4; wanting a thing so much it eats the fun, and what Harvey does about it, land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'sets his sights on winning a unique prize' omits the three misses, the fun-check intervention, and the flag ending. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Jack's bow tie collection is one orange short, and the carnival game is not cooperating: misses, near misses, and a parade of friends winning other prizes. Harvey notices the joy leaking out and rebuilds the day around rides and cotton candy before the last ticket. The final roll misses gloriously and somehow the collection completes itself anyway, with a flag that was never a prize at all.

rows.episode_title: Prize Bow Tie / Bread is Sleeping
rows.synopsis: Jack sets his sights on winning a unique prize at the carnival. While Robin's loaf of bread naps, the friends try to keep the noise down.
rows.situation: Bread needs a nap or Bread gets cranky, and every quiet game the friends invent turns loud: noisy pot-and-pan music, roaring airplane drawings, turkey dress-up. The retreat escalates from quiet play to far away to the moon, and Robin and Bread still hear everything.
rows.coping: After every plan fails, the friends name the pattern out loud, all our ideas turn out noisy, and try the one thing left: the quiet game. Bread wakes up happy instead of cranky, thanked by name, and the noise starts fresh on schedule.
rows.notes: mixed age: the lullaby-for-bread plays 2-4; the self-control of keeping quiet for someone else's need, after your own plans keep failing, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'try to keep the noise down' omits the moon chase, the cranky stakes, and the quiet-game finish. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Robin's loaf of bread is napping, and nap time is a moveable target for Harvey and Jack, whose quiet ideas keep breaking loud. They retreat across the park, underwater, and finally to the moon, and Bread sleeps through none of it, until the friends give up the fleeing and play the quiet game. The lullaby works, the nap holds, and Bread wakes up ready to play instead of cranky.

rows.episode_title: Harvey's Tattle Tail / Missing Mustache
rows.synopsis: Jinja helps Harvey stop his tail from wagging during hide-and-seek. Alan loses his mustache and worries he will never get it back.
rows.situation: Harvey's tail gives away every hiding spot by wagging at exactly the moments hide-and-seek gets exciting, so Jinja the ninja signs on as tail trainer. Peanut-butter-toast focus drills and sandy sweeping get him match-ready, and the big game at the farm undoes it all in one wag.
rows.coping: Harvey admits mid-game that his tail cannot stop, and Jinja flips the flaw: follow the wag, slow it down, and hide where a slow wag reads as scenery. The pair outlasts the whole seek team, and the tail that tattled becomes the strategy.
rows.notes: mixed age: the ninja training numbers play 2-4; a body part that will not obey, and turning the quirk into the trick, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'helps Harvey stop his tail from wagging' omits the training montage, the game-day failure, and that the ending works because the wag stays. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Harvey's tail cannot keep a secret, wagging at every exciting moment of hide-and-seek, so Jinja the ninja puts it through training: focus toasts, sand sweeping, mustache stealth missions. Game day at the farm scrambles it all, and the fix is not more discipline but a flip, use the wag, slow it, hide by it. The slowest tail in Sagoville wins the longest hide.

rows.episode_title: Harvey's Tattle Tail / Missing Mustache
rows.synopsis: Jinja helps Harvey stop his tail from wagging during hide-and-seek. Alan loses his mustache and worries he will never get it back.
rows.situation: Alan's mustache gets flung off by his own new invention, lands on a caterpillar named Miles, and Alan gives it away in the moment, then misses it immediately. The Mustache Finder combs Sagoville and finds everything that is not a mustache: tails, flowers, bananas, snow.
rows.coping: Alan says the regret out loud, I know I said you could keep it, but I miss it very much, and Miles hears him. The rainbow mustache Alan never wanted becomes Miles's best ever, and the old mustache goes home to the face that twirls it.
rows.notes: mixed age: the mustache-finder gags play 2-4; giving something away generously and then wanting it back, and the words that fix it, land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'loses his mustache' skips that Alan gives it away on purpose, regrets it, and works it out in words with Miles. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Alan's mustache takes flight on a new fetching invention and lands on Miles the caterpillar, who loves it so much Alan gives it away on the spot. Regret arrives fast, and the Mustache Finder tours every near-mustache in Sagoville without finding the one that matters. The fix is conversation and creativity: Miles trades up to a rainbow mustache, Alan gets his twirler back, and everyone keeps a friend.

rows.episode_title: Baby Harvey / Harvey Makes a Splash
rows.synopsis: Robin inspires Harvey to play pretend. Dewey, a darling water droplet, needs help finding a good place to splash.
rows.situation: Robin's baby game casts Harvey in the starring diaper, and he commits: high chair, bottle, bib, the works. But real life keeps being big, pizza slices, ski trips, and the big race are all things babies supposedly cannot do, and Robin's rules start shrinking the fun.
rows.coping: Robin fixes every problem herself by changing the game instead of the player: stroller skiing, a baby race invented on the spot. The pretend holds all the way to a crawling diaper race that Baby Harvey wins, and nobody had to stop being small to keep playing.
rows.notes: mixed age: the goo-goo-ga-ga comedy plays 2-4; the friend who holds the rules learning to bend them so a player can stay, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'Robin inspires Harvey to play pretend' omits the game-vs-fun negotiation and Robin's own inventive fixes. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Harvey joins Robin's baby game all the way in, diaper, high chair, bottle, and discovers babies are excluded from pizza, skiing, and races. Robin, holding the mommy role, chooses imagination over rules each time, a stroller that skis, a baby race invented for her friend, and the pretend grows bigger instead of ending.

rows.episode_title: Baby Harvey / Harvey Makes a Splash
rows.synopsis: Robin inspires Harvey to play pretend. Dewey, a darling water droplet, needs help finding a good place to splash.
rows.situation: Dewey the water droplet wants to splash with Harvey, and every splash lands on someone who did not sign up: Jinja's book, Ducky's wig, Gary's rainbow, a floating mustache. Harvey's promise to a new friend keeps colliding with everyone else's dry things.
rows.coping: Harvey learns the question that unlocks the whole town, may we splash here, please, and learns that not everybody wants to be wet. Fins supplies the splash philosophy and the sea, and the friends who got splashed show up at the beach once their own stuff was finished.
rows.notes: mixed age: the splash gags play 2-4; enthusiasm that keeps colliding with other people's boundaries, and asking before the wave, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'a darling water droplet needs help finding a good place to splash' hides the consent song structure and the friends' late arrival at the beach. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Harvey makes a friend made of water, and their friendship is one splash-width too wide for every place in Sagoville: books get soaked, wigs wilt, mustaches float away. The turn is a question, may we splash here, please, asked at sprinklers, tubs, and finally the sea. The beach works, and the splashed-upon friends arrive on their own schedule to join in.

rows.episode_title: A Little Fun / Toothbrush in Space
rows.synopsis: Peanuts offers to shrink Harvey and Jinja for a teeny-tiny party. Larry and Harvey blast off to help Jupiter with a pesky piece of broccoli in his teeth.
rows.situation: Harvey and Jinja are too big for the Squeakettes' birthday party games, watching the fun from outside it. Asking for a shrink spell is the ask-for-help move, and it comes with a catch: the magic only lasts a little while.
rows.coping: Being small opens a whole world of play, teapot slides and graham-cracker dancing, and when the magic wears off they are happy to be big again. The song lands the point: seeing things from a small point of view is worth the trip either way.
rows.notes: mixed age: the tiny-world wonder plays 2-4; the temporary-magic twist and big/small point-of-view framing land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'teeny-tiny party' omits the size-temporariness and the big-again ending. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Harvey and Jinja are too big for the Squeakettes' birthday games, so Peanuts shrinks them Squeakette-sized, with a timer on it. Small is its own adventure, the piñata falls to great small thinking, and when the spell wears off they take the lesson up a size: happy birthday works whether you are big or you are small.

rows.episode_title: A Little Fun / Toothbrush in Space
rows.synopsis: Peanuts offers to shrink Harvey and Jinja for a teeny-tiny party. Larry and Harvey blast off to rescue Jupiter's smile.
rows.situation: Jupiter has a problem that will not smile: space broccoli, stuck between planet-sized teeth. The fix needs a toothbrush the size of a sign, a rocket conversion, and one floss improvisation when the broccoli refuses to brush loose.
rows.coping: When brushing fails, Harvey and Larry do not pack up, they wing it, asking a passing space thingy for string. The floss frees the broccoli, the smile returns, and the toothpaste rocket heads home with the job done.
rows.notes: mixed age: the toothbrush rocket plays 2-4; a big job where plan A fails and plan B is improvised from what is around, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'Larry and Harvey blast off to rescue Jupiter's smile' omits the forgotten-floss beat and the wing-it rescue that actually works. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Space is smiling except for Jupiter, who has space broccoli wedged in planet-sized teeth. Harvey and Larry convert a toothbrush-store sign into the world's first toothbrush rocket ship, brush every tooth, and meet the problem that brushing cannot solve. Floss was forgotten on Earth, so space supplies its own string, and Jupiter's smile comes back full power.

rows.episode_title: Listen to the Shoe / Harvey Comes Undone
rows.synopsis: Jack, Harvey, and Binky make music with an unlikely instrument. Harvey's sweater unravels all over Sagoville.
rows.situation: A beach shoe plays music with no visible reason, and Binky's why has no bottom: guesses are not enough, and nobody actually knows. The scientific method arrives in preschool clothing, wash the sand out, check for an on button, and Juggo's shoe lore supplies the real clue, special shoes only work in pairs.
rows.coping: Nobody fakes an answer to the why: the friends stay curious, test one idea at a time, and follow the music back to the beach where the matching shoe waits in the sand. The mystery ends in a shoe duet owned by Cookie, with everyone invited to the concert.
rows.notes: mixed age: the dancing shoe gags play 2-4; curiosity as a method, guessing as a beginning not an ending, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'make music with an unlikely instrument' omits the full mystery structure and the pair-of-shoes reveal. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Binky asks why a beach shoe is making music, and the question outlasts every guess the friends can throw at it. Washing, buttons, and a shoe-store lesson narrow the mystery down to math: special shoes need their pair. The hunt leads back to the sand, the matching shoe turns up under a friend's toes, and the shoe music plays on with an audience.

rows.episode_title: Listen to the Shoe / Harvey Comes Undone
rows.synopsis: Jack, Harvey, and Binky make music with an unlikely instrument. Harvey's sweater unravels all over Sagoville.
rows.situation: Wilson knits Harvey the biggest, coziest sweater in Sagoville history, and Harvey loves it past the point of sense: nothing in the world could make him take it off. Then the sweater unravels mid-walk, and the yarn turns up one strand at a time in everyone else's projects.
rows.coping: Harvey tells Wilson the truth, you worked so hard and now my sweater is just yarn, and gives away strand after strand to Larry's web and Gary's jump rope because they make people happy. There is not enough left for a sweater, so Wilson knits the yarn that remains into a tail cozy, small, and exactly right.
rows.notes: mixed age: the yarn trail plays 2-4; losing a gift, generosity that costs something, and the smaller gift that fits, land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'Harvey's sweater unravels all over Sagoville' omits that Harvey chooses to let the yarn go piece by piece, and the tail-cozy ending. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Wilson's handmade sweater is Harvey's favorite thing in the world until one walk unknits it across the entire town. The trail leads through Larry's web and Gary's jump rope, and Harvey keeps giving the yarn away anyway, because each project makes someone happy. Wilson can only recover enough for something small, and the something small turns out to be perfect: a sweater, tailored for a tail.

rows.episode_title: Looking for Acorns / Rainbow Wishing Star
rows.synopsis: Robin and Harvey build a stunning snow castle, and accidentally bury Nutmeg's acorn stash. Harvey's snow castle becomes a plaything.
rows.situation: Nutmeg's acorn-powered plane needs her buried stash, and the treasure map of dance steps ends directly under the brand new snow castle that Robin and Harvey have not even played with yet. Pushing fails, Remy's snow boat tow cracks the towers, and the mission stalls between a friend's flight and a friend's castle.
rows.coping: Robin invents the compromise nobody thought of, smoosh the castle, play with it and wreck it in the same jump. The acorns surface, Nutmeg fuels up, and the whole crew rides to the mountain where her cousin has built a snow tube ride.
rows.notes: mixed age: the smoosh game plays 2-4; a want colliding with a want, solved by play instead of sacrifice, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'accidentally bury Nutmeg's acorn stash' omits the failed towing, the wreck-or-wait dilemma, and the smoosh-the-castle solution. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: The dance-step treasure map to Nutmeg's acorns ends under the snow castle Robin and Harvey just finished building. Every rescue plan damages something someone loves, until Robin turns the wreck into the game itself: smoosh the castle, from the top, with everyone. Acorns are freed, the plane flies, and the reward is a tube ride on a mountain with Nutmeg's cousin.

rows.episode_title: Looking for Acorns / Rainbow Wishing Star
rows.synopsis: Robin and Harvey build a stunning snow castle, and accidentally bury Nutmeg's acorn stash. Harvey's snow castle becomes a plaything.
rows.situation: Gary's biggest-ever rainbow accidentally anchors to a star and creates a wishing star with one wish per stripe. The wishes multiply across Sagoville for everyone but Harvey, who cannot think of a single thing to wish for himself, and the stripe count keeps dropping.
rows.coping: Harvey fills every stripe with other people's wishes until one remains, and the friends insist the last one is his. Looking at the empty patch of sky where the star came from, he finally knows: wish it home.
rows.notes: mixed age: the wish montage plays 2-4; generosity with a countdown, and a wish spent on letting go, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'Harvey's snow castle becomes a plaything' is the other story; tags anchor on segment_title plus the script. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Gary's record rainbow hooks a star and hands the friends a wishing star with a stripe for every wish. Wishes for Jack's paint, Nutmeg's wind, Robin's tea party, and half of Sagoville pour out, while Harvey, who started it, cannot find one wish of his own. The last stripe goes to the only wish he truly has: send the star back home to the sky.

rows.episode_title: Helping Hands / Leaf It to Harvey and Jinja
rows.synopsis: Wilson works hard on a cozy knitting project. Harvey and Jinja invite their friends to a special dinner.
rows.situation: Wilson cannot stop knitting until Miles's booties are done, which leaves no hands for gates, snacks, or high fives, and Harvey appoints himself the hands. Then the snow starts, and the helpers need helpers, until the whole town is one interlocking chain of jobs from tacos to waffles.
rows.coping: Nobody drops their own job to pitch in; each helper adds a link, Kiki plays the banjo so Neville can hold the hat so Harvey can feed Wilson, and the booties win the race against the snow. Wilson's thank-you is booties for everyone.
rows.notes: mixed age: the helper-chain song plays 2-4; how a favor for a friend ripples into a whole town helping, and hands busy with love needing hands, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'Wilson works hard on a cozy knitting project' omits the entire chain-of-helpers structure, which is the segment. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Wilson has knitted himself into a corner: booties for Miles before the snow, and no hands for anything else. Harvey becomes Wilson's hands, and one problem at a time recruits the whole town into a human (and ghost, and unicorn) chain where everyone's task frees someone else's hands. The booties arrive warm, the snow is caught on tongues, and everyone gets knitted thanks.

rows.episode_title: Helping Hands / Leaf It to Harvey and Jinja
rows.segment_title: Leaf It to Harvey and Jinja
rows.synopsis: Wilson works hard on a cozy knitting project. Harvey and Jinja invite their friends to a special dinner.
rows.situation: Miles's pool is a pile of leaves, and the invitation is hard to read: too chilly for Jack, too deep for the Squeakettes, and nobody swims in leaves. The party shrinks in real time, and then two clouds start blowing the pool away entirely.
rows.coping: Harvey rebuilds the pool around the complaints instead of the complaints around the pool, more leaves, shallower spots, a hot tub, a fountain. Even the leaf-blowing clouds get asked what they want, and end up flopping in.
rows.notes: mixed age: the leaf flop plays 2-4; an idea that does not fit everyone, and rebuilding it until it does, lands 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'Harvey and Jinja invite their friends to a special dinner' is the other story; tags anchor on segment_title plus the script. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Miles invites Harvey swimming in a pool that is entirely leaves, and the leaf pool party that follows is a masterclass in no: too chilly, too deep, too small, for different friends for different reasons. Harvey widens, warms, and shallows the pool until everyone has a way in, and when the leaf-blowing clouds threaten the whole thing, they get invited in too. Leaf flop.
